newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Regrade slides on cash pressure.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Regrade slides on cash pressure.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade was weaker at midday on Thursday after lower physical jet fuel trades on Tuesday, traders said.
"The regrade is under pressure from the physical trades at lower prices," one trader said.
June regrade was last quoted at minus 20 to minus 10 cents, about 5 cents lower than Tuesday while July was quoted at 10-20 cents, compared to 20-35 cents on Tuesday, brokers said.

The lower prices were due to the physical trades on Tuesday for two jet fuel cargoes at $24.25 per barrel for June 4-8 lifting of a 26,000-tonne cargo and at $24.60 for 100,000 barrels lifting June 15-19.
The deals were between 40-75 cents below the last deals done on MOnday, traders said.
The downward push on jet was expected as the second quarter is when demand is at its low and traders said they expected prices to fall further.
Gas oil swaps were steady with June swaps last quoted at $25.30/$25.50 per barrel.

Traders said the steady prices were a reflection of the range bound physical trading where two 150,000-barrel cargoes traded at $25.35 for mid-June lifting as the market moved back to an earlier firmly established $25.00-25.000 range.
Late last week, one cargo traded at $25.70 leading some to speculate that prices may have finally moved out of the month-long range but more sellers emerged and prices moved back down.
June fuel oil swaps were last quoted down alomost $1.00 despite strong physical buying support with two 20,000-tonne cargoes traded on Tuesday at $103.50 per tonne.
Traders said the market is discounting the buying support in the face of weak fundamental demand such as that from the bunker market and China.
June was last quoted at $101.00/$102.00 per tonne, down from Tuesday's $101.75/$102.50, brokers said.
